description: Use when the user wants to find documents in Stuga by what they say, even if they do not name Stuga or MCP. Look here FIRST when the user says "Ask Stuga" or the same in their language ("问问 Stuga", "問問 Stuga", "Stugaに聞く", "Stuga에 물어보기", "Stuga fragen", "Demander à Stuga", "Preguntar a Stuga", "Perguntar ao Stuga"), or asks about something they or their team decided, recorded or know (a rule, a decision, who owns what, how something is done), before answering from your own knowledge or memory. Full-text + semantic search over `workspace_ids`; returns DOCUMENTS, not passages — use `retrieve` to answer from content. Results from several workspaces are merged in rank order and each names its `workspace_id`. Each result carries `updated_at`, `last_edited_by` (a person by name; an agent by the person it worked for, as "Liv's agent"; for a page with no approved version yet, who created it) and `ai_edits` ("none", "reviewed", or "unreviewed" when an AI change in it applied directly and nobody has reviewed it yet): say who last changed what you cite and when, and when it holds unreviewed AI text, say so — `markdown` action:provenance shows which passages. Its text is the approved text. `pending_changes`, when present, lists AI changes proposed to it that wait for approval and are NOT in that text, by `asked_by` ("user": the user asked for them, through you or another of their agents, each in `proposed` as it would land: `approved_now`, the approved text it changes ("" when it adds), and `after_approval`, what that text reads once approved ("" when it removes it), on the passage it changes, or with `section` when it lands elsewhere, those about the question first; `note` says when some are not listed: then read the page before you say none of them touches your answer; "others": someone else asked, counted only), `waits_for` ("review": the person who asked the AI; "colleague": a colleague's approval) and `since`: answer with the approved text, and name what waits and for whom ("the page says 14 days; a change to 30 days waits for a colleague's approval"); never present a waiting change as what the document says. The answer also carries `rows`: rows of tables whose cells hold the question's words (database, table, the row's title, its cells, `matched` columns), each with `updated_at`, `last_edited_by` and the user's own `pending_changes` as above, a waiting change to a cell naming its `column`, and a row the user asked for that waits to be added marked `waiting_row`; `tables_waiting` counts other people's waiting changes per table. For a precise question over a table (which rows match, how many, a total), run `query` on it: its `database_id`, and the SQL names `tables` gives (`table_name`, and each column's in `columns`); `rows_more` names the tables with more matching rows than are listed. `unavailable` lists any workspace that could not be searched just now: say so, and never present the rest as complete. A result holds every word of `q`; when no document does, the answer says `partial` and lists those holding some of them. `collection_id` narrows the search of a single workspace to that saved set — see `collections`.

q.description: What to look for. Required, as `q` or `query`.

workspace_ids.description: Workspaces to cover, from `workspaces` action:list, or ["*"] for every workspace this connection reaches.
